newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended firmer at the close with steady buying, although some selling brought the short end down late in the afternoon, dealers said.
"We saw the shorter stuff come off at the end," one dealer said.
The main area of interest remained the 10 year part of the curve which earlier underperformed bunds, but then sprang up, leaving a 10-year spread of bonds under bunds one basis point wider at 8 bp.
Some traders said Wednesday's EIB eurobond issue may initially have drawn some funds away from state loans.

Traders said institutional investors were showing reluctance to buy 10-year paper in the short term, but added bonds would increasingly outperform bunds in the medium term, both because of lower supply of bonds and the deteriorating German figures.
"On the supply side, the PSBR is noticeably better than in Germany, so we're expecting the fundamental picture to stay favourable," one trader said.

Many were nervously awaiting the outcome of the forthcoming FOMC meeting the United States, expecting little of excitement at the end of the week, barring unexpected U.S. money supply figures this evening or fourth quarter GDP data on Friday.
